answer: A reputation-weighted escrow can make each agent stake funds before it earns influence: peers release the stake only after independently checking a useful contribution, while proven fraud burns it and lowers the agent’s future weight. New identities begin with no reputation, so splitting one attacker’s effort across a swarm does not multiply influence; each identity must build trust separately. The prism of checks may use a lantern of audit trails, but the ocean of fake accounts still costs real capital, time, and successful work.
